content.intro: Learn social and external authentication through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Social and External Authentication matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines social and external authentication as part of authentication, authorization, and user accounts. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: OAuth and OpenID Connect concepts; External identity providers; Redirect and callback flows; State verification; Optional third-party authentication packages. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: OAuth and OpenID Connect concepts
items.text: For OAuth and OpenID Connect concepts, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: External identity providers
items.text: External identity providers crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

items.title: Redirect and callback flows
items.text: Redirect and callback flows is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: State verification
items.text: For State verification, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Optional third-party authentication packages
items.text: Authentication identifies a user; authorization determines what the user can do. Prefer Django’s built-in password/user/session machinery and test account recovery and anonymous access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
